evidence: Closed-form and one-dimensional mechanics for two representative bodies (the dance body model and the same body scaled to 1.80 m and 80 kg) at the shared gravity and the design run's air, with stated parameter choices beside each figure. A screen of what a body can do for sport; the whole-body motion engine tests it, and the whole-body record (whole_body.json) measures what its solved motions did.

countermovement.note: a standing jump announces itself by its dip; a jump out of a landing (a rebound) needs none

flight.note: the centre of mass keeps its arc: shape changes orientation and turn rate; contact alone changes the arc

in_the_air.throw: chest pass, near the centre of mass
chest pass, near the centre of mass

throws.catches: a catch takes the same impulse in reverse: the tables hold for a ball caught at that speed

kick.note: what one foot cannot hold, the arms and trunk must take by turning against the leg

floor_and_falls.note: a change of height that must end at rest takes about twice as long as on Earth at either end: a body sinks no faster than g, and a rise slows no faster than g; one that ends in motion (a jump, a drop into a landing) is quick at its muscle end

microgravity.ground: no weight presses the feet: no grip, no stop, no turn without a surface to push against
microgravity.jumps: every push sets an endless drift; nothing returns a player to play
microgravity.balls: a ball flies straight until the air or a wall stops it; there is no arc to read
microgravity.falls: there is no falling, landing or getting up, and no down to play against
